name: Deng Xiaoping Theory
summary: Deng Xiaoping Theory is the Chinese Communist Party's guiding doctrine of the reform era. It keeps one-party rule, public ownership as the mainstay and Marxism-Leninism-Mao Zedong Thought as binding principles, while judging policy by whether it develops the productive forces. It accepts markets, foreign capital and some people getting rich first as tools of socialism, prefers gradual and stable change, and rejects Western-style democracy and separation of powers.
scope: The doctrine as set out in Deng's own speeches, 1978-1992 (Four Cardinal Principles, political reform, one country two systems, Southern Tour), and as summarised in Wikipedia's article. Excludes later additions by Jiang, Hu and Xi, and Mao-era positions Deng repudiated.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Deng's texts discuss growth and living standards but not a state healthcare guarantee; the reform era marketised health provision while the party still claims a socialist welfare aim, so adherents are split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Deng called planning and market 'both means' of developing productive forces and neither defining of socialism, so he rejects both a market-supremacy claim and a planning-supremacy claim.

public-ownership.rationale: Deng held that public ownership must remain the mainstay and defended the special zones as socialist because the public sector stays dominant, while allowing private and foreign firms alongside.

unions-good.rationale: Deng assigned unions a role of serving party-led modernisation, not independent bargaining; adherents would not endorse unions simply as good for workers against employers.

property-fundamental.rationale: Deng's framework keeps land and key industry in public hands and subordinates individual and local interests to collective ones, so private property is not a near-inviolable right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Deng welcomed private and foreign firms as useful supplements and favoured loosening controls, yet insisted on state direction of the economy; no clear position on tightening corporate regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Deng said socialism means eliminating poverty, which sits badly with welfare cuts, though his emphasis was growth rather than transfers.

worker-ownership.rationale: Deng pursued state, collective and private enterprise with managerial reform and gave no priority to worker-owned firms; he did propose worker participation in enterprise management (s4).

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Deng did not address hate speech; he did favour limits on speech that contravenes the Four Cardinal Principles, which is a different rationale.

strong-leader.rationale: Deng criticised over-concentration of power and the cult of personality and urged collective leadership, though he valued the system's ability to decide quickly.

state-harmful.rationale: Deng insisted on the people's democratic dictatorship and party-led state as the basis for socialism and modernisation; a stateless view is the opposite.

empower-police-military.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to police-more-powers: its rationale is about police powers, and this statement now asks only about military spending.

reviewHistory.rationale: Deng backed strict crackdowns on crime and, in 1989, martial law to secure stability, and also pushed to modernise the army.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to police-more-powers: its rationale is about police powers, and this statement now asks only about military spending.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

decide-locally.rationale: Deng devolved economic decision making to localities and zones but insisted on strong central authority and party unity.

rehabilitation.rationale: Deng stressed severe punishment of crime and economic crime, so adherents lean toward punishment, though reform through labour is an official theme.

traditional-family.rationale: The theory has no family doctrine; adherents are split between official socialist-ethics emphasis and modern change.

more-religion-public.rationale: Marxist atheism and party control over religion, with Deng's insistence on Marxism-Leninism, point against a larger public religious role.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not an issue in the theory; Deng backed equality of nationalities and accelerated development in minority regions but not remedial justice programmes.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The theory is silent; official Marxism gives some support to social explanations but adherents hold no settled view.

gradual-change.rationale: Deng said reform must proceed by small steps, with core policies kept stable for a long time, and that democracy advances step by step.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Deng stressed national sovereignty, opposed outside interference and wanted the five principles of peaceful coexistence as norms, not stronger supranational power.

free-trade.rationale: Deng pursued opening and foreign trade and investment as essential to modernisation, yet kept state control of the economy and special economic zones; he did not embrace free trade as doctrine.

nation-first.rationale: Deng said first priority belongs to national sovereignty and security, while also advocating opening and peace for development.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Deng opposed other countries interfering in China's internal affairs and promoted non-interference and peaceful coexistence as norms.

open-borders.rationale: Deng's insistence on sovereignty and on a state-managed opening rules out open borders as a goal.

limit-growth.rationale: Deng said socialism cannot endure in poverty and that developing the productive forces is the overriding task, so limiting growth is rejected.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate was not an issue in Deng's texts, and his priority on growth (s7) argues against drastic cuts, while a state-led approach would allow action; adherents are split.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Deng called science and technology a primary productive force and argued modernisation depends on them, though not that they solve most human problems.

revolution-justified.rationale: Deng owed his career to revolution but rejected Cultural Revolution turmoil and treated 'reform as revolution' only rhetorically; adherents split between historic revolution and stability.

experts-over-public.rationale: Deng urged respect for knowledge and trained personnel and technocratic appointment of cadres, with decisions led by the party rather than public opinion.

central-planning.rationale: Deng argued planning is not socialism and that markets can serve socialism, reversing Mao-era faith in planning as superior.

socialized-markets.rationale: Deng said markets are compatible with socialism if public ownership remains the mainstay, close to the statement's idea of public ownership alongside markets.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Deng did not address inheritance tax; he accepted private wealth accumulation while warning against polarisation.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Deng promoted opening and foreign technology but protected state industry in practice; no explicit stance.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Deng kept central authority and state control of key sectors while using markets; the party-state still guides strategic development.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Deng liberalised household farming and small business, yet kept land public and did not make wide property distribution a goal.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Deng rejected utopian leaps and advocated distribution according to work, a measure that keeps wages and money.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Deng's model is party-led, with market-set prices progressively replacing administered ones, not corporatist wage and price bargaining.

one-party-rule.rationale: The first Four Cardinal Principle is party leadership: Deng said there would be no socialist new China without the CCP and that socialism guided by Marxism-Leninism is the only road.

democracy-best.rationale: Deng rejected bourgeois individualist democracy and the Western model, preferring socialist democracy led by the party and judged by stability and results.

direct-votes.rationale: Deng wanted gradual expansion of grassroots democracy but never referendums on major laws; stability came first.

right-to-secede.rationale: Deng said Taiwan and Hong Kong belong to China under 'one country, two systems', and said sovereignty and security come first; no right of regions to leave.

political-violence-never.rationale: Deng defended force against hostile elements and martial law in 1989, and said Taiwan dispute may be settled by force if necessary.

war-builds-character.rationale: Deng argued China needed a peaceful environment for development and opposed hegemony, so glorifying war is not part of the theory.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Laws are to follow the Constitution and Marxism-Leninism-Mao Zedong Thought, not scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Deng's state monopolises security and law under party leadership; private provision is outside the theory.

military-superiority.rationale: Deng sought a modern army and defended sovereignty but rejected hegemony and put development first.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Deng's PRC is a multi-ethnic state, and the Four Cardinal Principles frame the state as a people's democratic dictatorship of all nationalities rather than one ethnic group.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Deng held class struggle continues in a changed form under socialism but moved focus to development and treated it as no longer the main task.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Deng held distribution according to work with some getting rich first, though common prosperity is the goal and polarisation is to be avoided.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Deng pressed no reparations claims; his line sought peaceful relations with former powers for development, so adherents have no settled view.

civilizational-union.rationale: Deng promoted peaceful coexistence among states of differing systems, not unions of civilisations.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Deng subordinated personal, local and short-term interests to collective, overall and long-term ones and rejected individualist democracy.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Deng said personal interests must yield to the collective and the whole, and that individualist freedoms cannot override the Four Cardinal Principles.

limit-population.rationale: Deng's era made population control a basic state policy, as population growth was seen to hinder development.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Deng's argument that socialism needs developed productive forces and that poverty is not socialism makes a negative verdict on industrialisation alien to the theory.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Deng urged learning advanced technology from abroad and taking China into high technology, within a stable political order.

restore-past-order.rationale: Deng rejected both leftist dogma and a return to the past, calling to emancipate the mind and push reform forward.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Deng judged policy by whether productive forces, living standards and national strength grow, and his 'seek truth from facts' pragmatism is the theory's signature.

direct-action.rationale: Deng treated unofficial groups, protests and wall posters as threats and emphasised order under party leadership.

means-match-ends.rationale: Deng defended pragmatic means including strong state action; he did not tie means to the end society.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Deng held socialism cannot be built on poverty, so a return to a pre-industrial life contradicts his premise that productive forces must keep developing.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Deng stressed specialist expertise, managerial skill and distribution by work, which keep the division of labour.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-10): its rationale calls need-based distribution the distant communist aim and balances it against the primary stage, which "ultimately" already allows for, so the sources cited here do not answer this statement.

reviewHistory.rationale: Deng held 'to each according to work' now and pursued common prosperity later; need-based distribution is a distant communist aim in the primary stage.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-10): its rationale calls need-based distribution the distant communist aim and balances it against the primary stage, which "ultimately" already allows for, so the sources cited here do not answer this statement.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

production-for-use.rationale: Deng defended socialism as raising living standards but allowed profit-seeking markets and firms as tools, so the pure claim is not endorsed.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: In the 1979 Four Cardinal Principles speech Deng states that socialism cannot be built or defended without the dictatorship of the proletariat, later called the people's democratic dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Rural reform under Deng broke up the commune in favour of household contracting while land stayed publicly owned, and the 1992 talks say rural reform policies must be kept stable.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Deng judged that world war could be avoided and that peace and development were the main trends, departing from the inevitable-war thesis.

taxation-theft.rationale: Deng held that the state must collect revenue and redistribute to poorer regions via taxes.

harm-principle.rationale: Deng's limits on speech and activity rest on the Four Cardinal Principles and stability, not only harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Deng put collective interests above individual ones; he also supported equality of nationalities, so group rights are not rejected.

conscription.rationale: The PRC's state with conscription law and Deng's concern for a modern, combat-effective army support it.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Deng treated emigration as no check on government; he stressed party leadership and domestic stability.

state-as-business.rationale: Deng borrowed market tools but treated the state as the party's instrument for socialism, not a service firm.

positive-liberty.rationale: Deng argued poverty is not socialism and that a rising standard of living is the test of a system, which loosely links freedom to material means.

organic-representation.rationale: The theory relies on people's congresses and party-led consultation; corporatist representation by family and trade is not part of it.

total-state.rationale: Deng wanted Party functions separated from government and enterprise management and cut bureaucratic overreach, although the party kept final political control.

national-rebirth.rationale: Deng spoke of revitalising the Chinese nation, and the later party line makes national rejuvenation its goal.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Deng said China would never seek hegemony and stressed peaceful reunification of Taiwan and Hong Kong rather than expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Deng criticised personal rule and called for institutional rules, collective leadership and retirement.

bound-labor.rationale: Peasant household contracts under Deng freed labour from commune obligation; bound labour contradicts this.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Deng's Marxism treats ideas as class-linked but also appeals to science and facts, so adherents are split.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Deng did not address a diaspora right of return; Overseas Chinese were courted for investment, but no principle of return is stated.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Deng wanted workers and staff congresses in enterprises, but within party leadership and manager responsibility.

school-vouchers.rationale: Deng said to run state education well and universalise it; vouchers are not part of his programme.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Deng wanted fast growth and also checked overheating; no stable doctrine on deficits.

economic-freedom.rationale: Deng rejected the claim that economic freedom leads to political freedom and kept party control while liberalising markets.

rule-by-example.rationale: Deng wanted cadres to set examples and follow fine party traditions but also stressed rules and law over reliance on moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Deng supported national independence and sovereignty and opposed outside interference, but denied it to regions inside China.

force-without-un.rationale: Deng opposed intervention and hegemony and upheld the five principles; he reserved force chiefly for national sovereignty questions.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about tradition, feeling, will or reason in general, not religious faith, which this statement now asks about.

reviewHistory.rationale: The party's scientific socialism and 'seek truth from facts' favour reason, though not as the only guide.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about tradition, feeling, will or reason in general, not religious faith, which this statement now asks about.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

work-for-welfare.rationale: Distribution according to work is Deng's principle, so work-linked benefits are consistent.

dominated-front.rationale: Deng promoted South-South cooperation but also friendship with the West, so no confrontational front.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The PRC's socialist order promotes women's equality; distinct legal roles are not part of the theory.

ban-interest.rationale: Deng reformed the banking system and promoted financial markets, so banning interest is rejected.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The theory presumes a unified state of equal citizens under the people's democratic dictatorship, so legal racial segregation has no place in it.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Deng's own formula, the dictatorship of the proletariat, treats the state as an instrument of class rule over hostile forces.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy claims of deliberate replacement have no place in a Marxist-Leninist line that stresses unity of nationalities.

proportional-representation.rationale: Deng rejected multi-party competition; the people's congresses system is not proportional.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Deng's texts do not analyse gender hierarchy; the Party claims women's equality but adherents do not hold a structural-patriarchy thesis as doctrine.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Deng admitted bureaucratism, privilege and corruption in the party and warned problems would come from within it, but did not call the elite as a whole corrupt.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Deng defended the 1989 martial law and the party's authority over the army and avoided accountability for past killings.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Deng's state leads economic development, directs reform and holds the dictatorship role; minimal government is the opposite.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Contradicts the policy of equality of nationalities.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Deng said all citizens are equal before the law, though he did not frame it as moral worth.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Deng's whole line is building socialism with Chinese characteristics in China alone, with no revolution abroad, and he opposed exporting revolution.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Marxist atheist state education provides no religious instruction.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Deng held that the dictatorship stays essential for socialism's defence and construction.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Deng claimed legitimacy from the party's record and the people's democratic dictatorship, not from a consent-based theory.

trade-surplus.rationale: Not a doctrine of Deng; export-led zones indicate openness to it.

population-transfer.rationale: Contrary to the equality-of-nationalities line and to the Hong Kong guarantees.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Deng said Taiwan could be settled by force if peaceful means fail.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Deng wanted market competition within socialism, but stressed unity and cooperation among peoples.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The Four Cardinal Principles bind party and state against attempts to overthrow the order.

separated-powers.rationale: Deng said China must not imitate the West and rejected Western separation of powers.

vanguard-party.rationale: The CCP is the vanguard of the working class and central leader of socialist construction, per Deng's first principle.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Deng said poverty is not socialism and that eliminating poverty is a duty to uphold socialism.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Independent labour action was suppressed; stability prime.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Deng's family planning rationale was that population growth held back living standards.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The official line stresses the unity of a multiethnic nation.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Deng's cadres are selected by the party for competence and age.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Deng ordered martial law in 1989 and said China would tolerate no disturbances.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Deng liberalised prices gradually but kept control over essentials.

party-controls-media.rationale: Deng demanded the press follow the Four Cardinal Principles and opposed bourgeois liberalisation.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party leadership is the second pillar of the Four Cardinal Principles and Deng himself held the chair of the Party's Central Military Commission, so command by the Party is the settled arrangement.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Deng opposed cadre privileges but accepted wage differentials.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Deng urged discipline and unity of ideals and majority-rule voting in Party committees with decisions then binding on all members.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Deng stressed national sovereignty and independence.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Command lies with the party's military commission.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is outside Deng's concerns, apart from state supervision of religion in general.

clerical-rule.rationale: Incompatible with Marxism-Leninism and party leadership.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Deng stressed patriotism and national defence; a defeatist line is not endorsed.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Deng promised creative freedom for writers within socialist direction, and also opposed harmful bourgeois tendencies.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Deng opposed life tenure and called for term limits and retirement for cadres.

recall-officials.rationale: Mass supervision was endorsed, but there is no recall tradition.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Deng adopted an independent foreign policy and non-alignment and rejected alliances.

people-in-arms.rationale: Deng pushed to streamline and modernise a professional army (s7 stresses technology), which is the opposite of replacing it with an armed citizenry.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Deng placed reunification of the mainland and Taiwan on the agenda and proposed one country, two systems.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Deng's reform emphasis on science, technology and expertise (s7, s1) treats educated people as an asset to the Party, not as a detached class.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Deng's texts do not rank cultures; his insistence on a Chinese road (s7) is compatible with both relativism and national pride.

death-penalty.rationale: Deng urged cracking down hard on crime, with severe punishment.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Anti-spiritual-pollution campaigns followed his call for high ethical standards.

minority-language-support.rationale: Deng backed equality of nationalities and development in minority regions.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Deng said follow our own road in economic development as in revolution.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Deng ruled out Western democracy and multi-party competition.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Deng said the overriding need is stability, and that growth takes priority over liberal political demands.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Deng stressed self-reliance and South-South cooperation but also sought foreign aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The PRC under Deng retained its own nuclear forces.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Deng rejected Western-style democracy and the separation of powers (s4) and the head of state is chosen within the Party-led system.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Deng reformed the banking system under party-state guidance.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Deng claimed sovereignty over territory and refused concessions on it.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Deng subordinated private interests to collective ones.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Deng criticised past errors but didn't adopt this theory.

collective-defense.rationale: Deng pursued an independent foreign policy and avoided bloc alliances, so automatic collective-defence commitments are not part of his line.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Marxism-Leninism and Party leadership (s2) place religious institutions under state supervision, which matches this statement's direction.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Deng said that if a dispute over reunification cannot be settled peacefully it may be resolved by force, while preferring peaceful means.

region-keeps-system.rationale: This is Deng's one country, two systems: Hong Kong and Taiwan keep their systems for 50 years.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The Party line rejects the cult of personality, as Deng stated in 1980, and a sacred hereditary ruler is incompatible with Marxism-Leninism.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Deng said officials are bound by law like all citizens.

space-expansion.rationale: Deng backed high technology and defence science but did not name space as a central goal of civilisation.

leader-cult.rationale: Deng criticised the cult of personality and lavish honouring of leaders.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family law details lie outside Deng's texts and adherents have no settled view.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Deng held that class struggle survives in a limited form but rejected Mao's thesis that party leaders were restoring capitalism, under which he had been purged; the 1981 Resolution repudiated continuing revolution.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land reform was completed; Deng chose household contracts over redistribution.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The Party is Marxist-atheist and treats religion as a matter of private belief under state supervision, so punishing leaving a religion is not part of its approach.

women-must-cover.rationale: A dress mandate on women has no basis in Deng's socialist legal order, which stresses equality of all citizens before the law.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Deng's thesis that developing the productive forces is the essence of socialism rests on the Marxist view that the material base drives social development.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Deng held officials must be bound by law (s6) but also denied independent courts; no clear position on majority rule over institutions.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Deng's defining policy was opening to the outside world, with special economic zones, foreign capital and technology, the reverse of an autarkic bloc.

moral-incentives.rationale: Deng restored material incentives, with distribution according to work, and criticised egalitarian poor socialism that relied on exhortation.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Deng came from a revolution built on an armed party, but in the reform era treated revolution as finished and prioritised stability.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Deng attacked cadre privileges and life tenure in 1980 and called for equality before the law, which opposes inherited status.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Deng framed China as a former victim of imperialism and urged non-interference and equal coexistence between states.

patriotic-education.rationale: Deng required adherence to the Four Cardinal Principles as a basis for unity, and the later line makes patriotic education central.

public-money-creation.rationale: Deng reformed the banking system toward a more commercial footing but did not address who creates money.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Deng judged that peace and development were the world's main trends and that capitalist countries have strengths to learn from, departing from collapse-of-capitalism orthodoxy.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not part of Deng's line; he told China never to seek hegemony.

delink-world-market.rationale: Deng's opening policy integrated China into the world economy, the opposite of delinking.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Deng wanted law that binds officials but kept citizens' freedoms subordinate to the Four Cardinal Principles.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Deng treated the unequal treaties' legacy through negotiation of Hong Kong, not through general voiding.

elective-rulers.rationale: Deng rejected Western-style elections for choosing national rulers, keeping party-selected leadership.

minority-veto.rationale: Deng held that the minority in Party committees follows the majority.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Deng wanted law to bind leaders but located correction within party organisations, not popular resistance.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Deng placed the Party above state organs, though the people's congresses are the formal legislature.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal welfare is absent from Deng's texts, with no basis for a direction.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Deng's some-get-rich-first line said the better-off regions should later help poorer ones, a state duty rather than a noble one.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Deng called on all to join in building socialism under Party leadership.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Deng sought integration into the world economy for gain, a view opposed to dependency theory.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Deng stressed following our own road yet sought foreign funds, loans and technology.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Deng sought return of Hong Kong and reunification with Taiwan as lost territory.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Deng's ethnic policy used autonomous regions with party-led cadres, without a doctrine on descendants of pre-colonial peoples.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A US historiographical dispute outside Deng's concerns.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Deng addressed leader cults (s6) but not contested monuments generally, so no direction.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Gender-specific disadvantage is outside Deng's texts; no direction inferable.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Outside Deng's texts, with no direction inferable.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Deng said China must not imitate the West and must build socialism with Chinese characteristics suited to Chinese conditions.

office-by-exam.rationale: Deng pushed promotion of trained, younger cadres by competence, not birth.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Deng kept the public sector as mainstay and state control of strategic industries while admitting foreign firms as supplements.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Deng's reform proposals expand mass supervision but do not bind leaders to recall.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land stays owned by the state or collectives while households hold use rights, which matches Deng's rural reform.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Not part of Deng's model of the Party-led state.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land is public property in the PRC, so foreigners cannot own it, even as they invest.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Not part of Deng's frame; some regions were to get rich first.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Deng wanted rising living standards as the test of socialism (s7) while the party also stresses ethical standards, so adherents are split.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Deng reversed support for foreign revolutions, saying China would not interfere in others' affairs.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Deng's era restricted births to ease population pressure.

job-guarantee.rationale: Deng broke the iron rice bowl of guaranteed jobs and promoted enterprise reform.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Deng demanded observance of law and Party authority and said officials too must obey law.

non-intervention.rationale: Deng held that China would not allow other countries to interfere in its internal affairs and promoted the five principles of peaceful coexistence as norms.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is outside Deng's texts, and the official ACFTU is Party-run; no direction inferable.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy against nation is not part of the line.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Deng demanded the press follow the Four Cardinal Principles and not weaken party authority.

local-production.rationale: Deng's opening and export zones push integration with markets elsewhere.

informal-organisation.rationale: Deng treated unofficial groups outside Party control as threats to stability (s2), so organising struggle in informal groups is rejected.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Deng stressed national sovereignty over the supranational and international.

religious-nation.rationale: The nation is defined by socialist citizenship and nationalities, not a shared religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Deng said China would never seek hegemony and insisted on equality among nations.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Deng said richer regions should transfer taxes and profits to poorer ones.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Even under Deng's public mainstay, personal belongings and income stay private.

defeat-communism.rationale: Deng called for peaceful coexistence of social systems while upholding socialism.

religion-illusion.rationale: Marxist-atheist outlook is official but Deng stressed non-confrontation and no stated claim about religion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Deng called for learning from capitalism's technology and management and said capitalist methods can serve development.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Deng's texts do not link gender equality to economic transformation, though Marxist orthodoxy might; adherents are split.

socialized-care.rationale: Deng's reform pushed enterprises and households to take more responsibility, while official socialism claims welfare aims; no clear stance.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Deng stressed learning from foreign countries.

treaties-binding.rationale: Deng stressed honoring international commitments (Hong Kong guarantees, s5) but did not address treaties with internal nations.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Deng's priority is large-scale modernisation under party-state leadership.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Deng held that socialism with Chinese characteristics is the answer, not a third way.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Deng said China would tolerate no disturbances, and treated unofficial groups and open attacks on the Party as threats to be dealt with.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Deng wanted China never to seek hegemony and framed China as a victim of imperialism, so governing colonies for the metropole is rejected.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Religious legitimacy is outside the Party line.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Deng sought broader mass supervision and workers' roles in management but within party leadership.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Intersectional analysis is absent in Deng's texts, with no direction inferable.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Gender identity is absent from Deng's texts and was not a Party issue in his period.

assisted-dying.rationale: End-of-life law is not in Deng's texts; adherents have no settled view.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Deng framed the main dangers as Left and Right errors, so the division is not obsolete.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not part of Deng's equality of nationalities line.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Deng grounded Hong Kong and Taiwan claims in sovereignty over territory historically Chinese.

rich-first.rationale: Deng said some regions should develop first and later help poorer ones.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Marxist-Leninist atheism and the Four Cardinal Principles place authority in the Party leading the people, with no divine source.

social-market-economy.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about regulation, competition or state direction, not a public safety net, which this statement now asks about.

reviewHistory.rationale: Deng called planning and market both means, with public ownership as mainstay and state macro-control, which is a regulated market rather than laissez-faire or full state running.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about regulation, competition or state direction, not a public safety net, which this statement now asks about.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Deng pushed to modernise the army and kept Party control of the military, and treated force as a last resort for sovereignty, not as something to give up.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Deng attacked life tenure, over-concentrated power and feudal habits in the leadership, so hereditary succession in office runs against his reforms.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Deng stressed self-reliance and sovereignty yet also opened China to World Bank and foreign capital; he never addressed lender conditions directly, so adherents are split.

property-franchise.rationale: Deng's socialist democracy is a broad-franchise system for the people; a property or tax qualification contradicts it.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Deng dismissed bourgeois freedoms as freedoms for the propertied, which matches the claim that wealth owning the presses empties press freedom.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Deng called for making democracy institutionalised and legalised and for equality before the law, though under party leadership.

racial-franchise.rationale: The theory upholds equal nationalities and regional autonomy for minorities; an ethnic franchise has no place in it.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The doctrine stresses unity of all nationalities; a boycott of a religious minority's shops would breach that line.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Deng accepted some getting rich first but warned against polarisation and favoured common prosperity; he did not frame wealth concentration as a threat to liberty.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The Four Cardinal Principles stress the dictatorship and stability, and Deng saw police and legal order as essential to preserving it.

term-limits.rationale: Deng argued that no leader should hold office for life and that cadres should retire, which supports tenure limits.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Marxism-Leninism is materialist and Deng judged politics by productive forces and stability, so a cosmic spiritual struggle is foreign to the doctrine.

god-not-male.rationale: The Party is atheist and indifferent to doctrinal language about God; neither answer is part of the doctrine.

independent-unions.rationale: The Four Cardinal Principles make Party leadership non-negotiable, so unions work as Party-led bodies, not independent ones.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The Four Cardinal Principles define the state as a people's democratic dictatorship led by the working class through its Party; an adherent affirms this in the formal sense, though real power rests with the Party.

second-chamber.rationale: Deng rejected Western separation of powers and kept a single-chamber National People's Congress under Party leadership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Deng stressed centralised leadership, stability and democratic centralism, which leaves no room for local assemblies that decide while delegates only coordinate.

person-over-state.rationale: Deng subordinated individual rights to collective and national interests and to the Four Cardinal Principles.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Deng spoke of building a socialist spiritual civilisation alongside material progress, but within a Marxist materialist framework, so adherents are split on the literal claim.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Deng stressed unity of the nationalities under Party leadership, so organising by race to defend group interests runs against it; the issue is framed as nationalities, not race.

racial-pride.rationale: Patriotism and national pride are strongly encouraged, but pride in race or ancestry as such is not a theme in the sources.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Deng rejected overthrowing the system and wanted the Party to reform the state, separating Party from government without separation of powers.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Deng said some regions should get rich first and later help poorer ones, and warned against polarisation, which frames regional gaps as a stage in development.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Four Cardinal Principles make the Communist Party the sole leader and reject separate parties, so an independent workers' party is excluded.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Deng's texts do not address union membership terms; Party-led unions make the question one of administration, so adherents are split.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The Four Cardinal Principles keep religion under Party leadership; the state recognises several faiths but guides them, so adherents are split.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Deng judged a political system by stability, unity and productivity and rejected Western multiparty elections and separation of powers.

women-suffrage.rationale: Equal political rights for women are established in the PRC constitution that Deng's doctrine upholds, and nothing in the doctrine disputes them.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The Four Cardinal Principles uphold Marxism-Leninism, which does not accept scripture as inerrant truth.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Deng defends the socialist road and warns against capitalist restoration while criticising bureaucracy as a flaw to reform.

national-church-status.rationale: The Four Cardinal Principles keep a secular, atheist state with no privileged national church.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Deng's one country, two systems and the existing ethnic autonomy system give autonomy to regions within a unitary state.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Deng treated the status of Taiwan and Hong Kong as questions for governments and negotiation, not a local vote.

simple-living.rationale: Deng said poverty is not socialism and urged getting rich and developing the productive forces, not austerity.

close-ties-china.rationale: Deng's opening-up policy favoured wide economic ties, including with China's partners, but he did not frame it as an alternative to the United States.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Deng's one country, two systems addressed Taiwan and Hong Kong, not kin minorities in neighbouring states.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Deng defended Party leadership as one of the Four Cardinal Principles and said political reform must not weaken it.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Marxist orthodoxy is retained as a binding principle, but Deng's texts do not discuss the theory itself.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Deng links patriotism with socialism and the unity of the nation under the Four Cardinal Principles and the one country, two systems framework.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Deng stated that markets exist under socialism and that a planned economy is not socialism, while the party keeps leadership.

police-more-powers.rationale: Deng backed strict crackdowns on crime and, in 1989, martial law to secure stability, and also pushed to modernise the army. (Moved from empower-police-military, 2026-11-11, when that statement became about military spending alone.)

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Deng said socialism means eliminating poverty, which sits badly with welfare cuts, though his emphasis was growth rather than transfers. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

former-empire-equal-treatment.rationale: Not part of Deng's line; he told China never to seek hegemony. (Carried over from former-empire-influence, "A country should cultivate political and cultural influence in regions once ruled by its predecessor empire.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: A country may let some regions and people get rich first so that others follow.
missingStatements.rationale: Deng said some regions should develop first and later help poorer ones, warning against polarisation.

missingStatements.text: Markets and economic planning are both only tools, and neither defines a social system.
missingStatements.rationale: Deng stated that a planned economy is not socialism because capitalism also has planning, and that markets exist under socialism.

missingStatements.text: Officials should be limited to fixed terms and retire, with no one holding office for life.
missingStatements.rationale: Deng said no leading cadre should hold any office indefinitely.

missingStatements.text: Open, foreign-invested special economic zones can serve a country's development without abandoning its political system.
missingStatements.rationale: Deng defended the special zones and foreign firms as useful supplements while public ownership remains the mainstay.
missingStatements.declined: Special economic zones are specific to China; free-trade and delink-world-market cover the openness axis.

notes: Answers about Deng's practice versus later Party lines (Jiang, Xi) can differ; the profile follows Deng's own texts. Many social-issue statements were not addressed by Deng and are low confidence.
